AGENTS.md

Source: AGENTS.md

Guidance for AI coding agents helping people use evomod2, an R package (C++ core via Rcpp/RcppArmadillo) for individual-based simulations of multivariate trait evolution: genetic architectures, mutation, recombination, selection regimes and G/M matrix statistics.

Documentation: https://diogro.github.io/evomod2/. Start from the vignettes; they are the best source of working code.

Using the package

Install

remotes::install_github("diogro/evomod2", build_vignettes = TRUE)

A C++ compiler is required (Xcode command line tools on macOS, Rtools on Windows).

The workflow

Every simulation is a model, a list of regimes, and evolve():

library(evomod2)
model <- evomod_model(
  architecture = additive(loci = 50, traits = 4),
  mutation = mutation(rate = 0.0005, cov = 0.2),   # cov: a matrix, or a number = sd per trait
  env_sd = 0.8,
  init_sd = 0.1,
  recombination = free_recombination(),           # default
  life_cycle = wright_fisher())                   # default
pop <- evolve(model, n = 1000, record_every = 50, seed = 1,
              regimes = list(drift(500),
                             stabilizing(2000, omega = 10),
                             directional(2000, delta_theta = c(0.01, 0.01, 0, 0), omega = 10)))
pop <- evolve(pop, stabilizing(500, omega = 10))  # continue the same population

Read results with trait_means(), variances(), g_matrices(), p_matrices(), mean_fitness(), plot(pop). Analyse with avg_corr(), autonomy(), mean_autonomy(), eigen_variance(), g_decomposition(), additive_covariance(), mutational_covariance(), local_effects().

Components (pick one of each)

Component Options
Architecture additive(), binary_b(), multilinear() (shared tensor from random_epsilon(), or one tensor per pair of loci from pairwise_epsilon()), contribution_matrix()
Mutation mutation() / hoc_mutation() for additive and multilinear; binary_b_mutation() for binary_b(); contribution_mutation() for contribution_matrix() (the model checks the match)
Recombination free_recombination(), genetic_map(chromosomes, length), linkage(rates)
Life cycle wright_fisher() (discrete generations), moran() (overlapping), viability_selection() (sexes, viability selection; Jones et al.)
Regimes drift(), stabilizing(), directional(), fluctuating()

Conventions that are easy to get wrong

  • Standard deviations, not variances. env_sd, init_sd, the sd arguments and a scalar mutational cov are standard deviations; a matrix cov is a covariance matrix. omega is a covariance matrix (a scalar means omega * I). Fitness is exp(-(z - theta)' omega^-1 (z - theta) / 2).
  • Rates are per allele (or per entry of B) per generation. A diploid locus has two alleles, so the expected number of mutations per genome is rate * 2 * loci (see mutational_covariance(pop)$expected_mutations).
  • Genomes are arrays rows x alleles x individuals (genomes(pop)); alleles 2l - 1 and 2l are the paternal and maternal copies of locus l. Rows are the effect vector (one per trait), except for binary_b() (y, then the column of B) and contribution_matrix() (one scalar).
  • The optimum carries over between regimes and between evolve() calls; a regime resets it only when given theta. directional() moves it before selection in every generation; fluctuating() jumps after every every generations.
  • Records are taken every record_every generations (and at the start of a new population); the first record is generation 0. Moments are recorded after the generation’s reproduction.
  • persistence in the mutation functions: 1 (default) is a random walk, 0 the house of cards model.
  • g_decomposition() is exact only for architectures whose genotypic values are sums of allele effects (additive(), binary_b()); for the others use method = "shuffle".
  • additive_covariance() needs more individuals than loci x traits.
  • Moran drift is about twice as strong per generation as Wright-Fisher at the same n (N_e is about n / 2).
  • Binary B mutation: b_mutation = "flip" (default) always changes a mutated entry; "random" reproduces the original C code of Melo & Marroig (2015), where entries changed at half the nominal rate.

Reproducibility

Random numbers come from R’s generator: seed = (or set.seed()) makes a run reproducible, and continuing a population in several evolve() calls gives the same result as one call. When running replicates in parallel, give each its own seed.

Running many replicates

The examples in system.file("examples", package = "evomod2") run replicated experiments from the command line, one replicate per process (Rscript <script> <mode> ... <outdir>, then a summarise mode). Use that pattern for large experiments: one single-threaded process per replicate, started with OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS=1 OMP_NUM_THREADS=1 MKL_NUM_THREADS=1 so that multithreaded BLAS does not oversubscribe the machine. Typical costs: a few seconds for 1000 individuals with 20 loci and 4 traits over 5000 generations; about 0.25 s per generation for 5000 individuals with 500 loci and 10 traits (2 GB of memory).

Published results reproduced in the vignettes

  • vignette("melo-marroig-2015"): directional selection and modularity.
  • vignette("fluctuating-environments"): do O & Whitlock (2023) across architectures.
  • vignette("jones-burger-arnold-2014"): epistasis and the evolution of M.

Each states the parameters used and where evomod2 differs from the original simulations. Point users to them before re-deriving those setups.

Changing the package

Agents extending or modifying evomod2 itself (new architectures, mutation models, regimes, analyses) should read DEVELOPMENT.md.
